title: Registering Additional Source Files
subtopics: Setting a custom source base path
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of registering additional source files.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on registering additional source files and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: The reliability of registering additional source files affects whether Tailwind detects candidate classes and generates the CSS you expect at build time.

content_blocks.title: Module 4 learning map
content_blocks.alt_text: Four-step module learning map: Understanding Utility-Class Naming → Understanding Variants → Handling Dynamic Class Names Correctly → Establishing a Reliable Utility-Class Workflow. Lesson pages add code examples and practice.
content_blocks.caption: Learning map for Module 4, from the opening concept to a practical checkpoint.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Using the @source directive; Registering external component libraries; Setting a custom source base path; Disabling automatic detection when necessary; Excluding unwanted paths. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to registering additional source files, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating registering additional source files. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to registering additional source files.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to registering additional source files.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: The shared package is explicitly registered so Tailwind can detect its utility tokens.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying registering additional source files without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Registering Additional Source Files is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
